measures.label: Crime exposure
measures.subcopy: Police-recorded crime relative to the U.S., adjusted for the people, premises or vehicles present. Not an individual's probability.

measures.label: Per resident
measures.subcopy: Police-recorded crime per resident relative to the U.S.

rob.exposure: Relative risk of robbery for the people present (residents, daytime population and workers), 100 = U.S. average. The level is the police agency's recent robbery total (two-year half-life, matched to the FBI's 2025 state estimate); the share within the agency comes from mapped police incidents in the cities that publish them and from a statistical model elsewhere.
rob.resident: Expected robbery offenses divided by the people who live here, relative to the U.S. Places with many visitors and few residents, such as shopping districts, score high on this measure.

agg.exposure: Relative risk of aggravated assault for the people present (residents, daytime population and workers), 100 = U.S. average. The level is the police agency's recent aggravated assault total (two-year half-life, matched to the FBI's 2025 state estimate); the share within the agency comes from mapped police incidents in the cities that publish them and from a statistical model elsewhere.
agg.resident: Expected aggravated assault offenses divided by the people who live here, relative to the U.S. Places with many visitors and few residents, such as shopping districts, score high on this measure.

lar.exposure: Relative risk of larceny/theft for the people and places here: half people present, 30% destination places (shops, restaurants, venues), 20% retail jobs. The level is the police agency's recent larceny/theft total (one-year half-life, matched to the FBI's 2025 state estimate); the share within the agency comes from mapped police incidents in the cities that publish them and from a statistical model elsewhere.
lar.resident: Expected larceny/theft offenses divided by the people who live here, relative to the U.S. Places with many visitors and few residents, such as shopping districts, score high on this measure.

bur.exposure: Relative risk of burglary per premises: households, group-quarters residents (0.27 premises each), destination places and retail and industrial jobs, weighted by a fit to mapped burglaries. The level is the police agency's recent burglary total (one-year half-life, matched to the FBI's 2025 state estimate); the share within the agency comes from mapped police incidents in the cities that publish them and from a statistical model elsewhere.
bur.resident: Expected burglary offenses divided by the people who live here, relative to the U.S. Places with many visitors and few residents, such as shopping districts, score high on this measure.

mvt.exposure: Relative risk of vehicle theft per vehicle present: household vehicles plus commuters' cars, and never fewer than 0.25 vehicles per person present. The level is the police agency's recent motor vehicle theft total (one-year half-life, matched to the FBI's 2025 state estimate); the share within the agency comes from mapped police incidents in the cities that publish them and from a statistical model elsewhere.
mvt.resident: Expected motor vehicle theft offenses divided by the people who live here, relative to the U.S. Places with many visitors and few residents, such as shopping districts, score high on this measure.

mur.exposure: Murders are too rare for one year's count in a neighborhood to show its risk, so this is a smoothed estimate for the census tract, per person present: the agency level weights recent years with a one-year half-life and leans on similar agencies when the agency is small, and the tract share comes from the city's own murders since 2018 (10-year half-life) anchored to its pattern of violent incidents (in the cities that publish incidents) or from a statistical model elsewhere. Read it as where murder risk is concentrated; in a small town one murder can move the value several-fold.
mur.resident: The same smoothed tract murder estimate divided by residents instead of people present. Places with many visitors and few residents, such as shopping districts, score high on this measure.

rap.exposure: Rape is also too rare to read from one year, so this is a smoothed census-tract estimate per person present: the agency level averages about five years (two-year half-life) and the tract share comes from a statistical model nearly everywhere. Reporting and definitions of rape vary across agencies more than for other offenses.
rap.resident: The same smoothed tract rape estimate divided by residents instead of people present. Places with many visitors and few residents, such as shopping districts, score high on this measure.

ov.exposure: The seven offense indexes averaged with weights equal to each offense's share of U.S. offenses (larceny/theft 61%, aggravated assault 13%, motor vehicle theft 11%, burglary 10%, robbery 3%, rape 2%, murder 0.2%), so it mostly reflects the frequent property crimes.
ov.resident: Expected offenses of all seven offenses added up and divided by residents, relative to the U.S.; each offense counts by its number of offenses (larceny/theft 61%, aggravated assault 13%, motor vehicle theft 11%, burglary 10%, robbery 3%, rape 2%, murder 0.2%). Places with many visitors and few residents, such as shopping districts, score high on this measure.

vi.exposure: Murder, rape, robbery and aggravated assault indexes averaged with weights equal to their share of U.S. violent offenses (aggravated assault 72%, robbery 15%, rape 11%, murder 1%).
vi.resident: Expected offenses of the four violent offenses added up and divided by residents, relative to the U.S.; each offense counts by its number of offenses (aggravated assault 72%, robbery 15%, rape 11%, murder 1%). Places with many visitors and few residents, such as shopping districts, score high on this measure.

pr.exposure: Burglary, larceny/theft and vehicle-theft indexes averaged with weights equal to their share of U.S. property offenses (larceny/theft 74%, motor vehicle theft 13%, burglary 13%).
pr.resident: Expected offenses of the three property offenses added up and divided by residents, relative to the U.S.; each offense counts by its number of offenses (larceny/theft 74%, motor vehicle theft 13%, burglary 13%). Places with many visitors and few residents, such as shopping districts, score high on this measure.

copy.source_mostly_direct: Mostly from local police incident records

copy.total_estimated: Jurisdiction total: estimated, not reported in full for 2025
